title: Regular -er verbs in the present
summary: Most French verbs end in -er. Drop the -er and add -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. Three of those endings are silent.
focus: Conjugating regular -er verbs in the present tense
content:
## One pattern for thousands of verbs

Nine French verbs out of ten end in **-er**. Take off the **-er** to get the stem (**parl-**), then add the ending for the person:

| | parler (to speak) | ending |
|---|---|---|
| je | parle | -e |
| tu | parles | -es |
| il / elle / on | parle | -e |
| nous | parlons | -ons |
| vous | parlez | -ez |
| ils / elles | parlent | -ent |

The endings **-e**, **-es** and **-ent** are **silent**: **je parle**, **tu parles** and **ils parlent** sound exactly the same. Only **nous parlons** and **vous parlez** sound different.

## Elision and liaison

When the verb starts with a vowel or a silent **h**, **je** becomes **j'**:

- **J'habite à Lyon.** (I live in Lyon.)
- **J'aime le chocolat.** (I like chocolate.)
- **J'écoute la radio.** (I listen to the radio.)

After **nous**, **vous**, **ils** and **elles**, the final **s** links to the vowel with a **z** sound (the *liaison*): **ils aiment** sounds like *il-z-aiment*, **nous habitons** like *nou-z-habitons*. Compare **il aime** (no z) and **ils aiment** (z). The liaison is the only way to hear the plural.

## Nous mangeons and verbs in -ger

In verbs ending in **-ger**, the **g** must stay soft before **-ons**, so the **nous** form keeps an **e**:

- **nous mangeons** (we eat), never *mangons*
- **nous nageons** (we swim)
- **nous voyageons** (we travel)

Every other form is regular: **je mange**, **vous mangez**, **ils mangent**.

## Aimer + infinitive, and verbs to know

To say you like *doing* something, put the second verb in the infinitive, straight after **aimer**:

- **J'aime danser.** (I like dancing.)
- **Nous aimons regarder des films.** (We like watching films.)

Common -er verbs follow the same pattern: **regarder** (to watch), **écouter** (to listen to), **étudier** (to study), **jouer** (to play), **travailler** (to work), **danser** (to dance). Note that **écouter** and **regarder** need no word for *to* or *at*, as in **j'écoute la radio** and **je regarde la télé**.

quiz.explanation: The nous form ends in -ons: nous parlons.

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct sentence: 'I live in Marseille.'
quiz.explanation: Habiter starts with a silent h, so je becomes j', and the je ending is -e: j'habite.
hints: The h of habiter is silent.

quiz.explanation: Verbs in -ger keep an e before -ons so the g stays soft: nous mangeons.
hints: The g must sound like the s in 'pleasure'.

quiz.prompt: In 'ils aiment', you hear a z sound between ils and aiment.
quiz.explanation: That is the liaison: the silent s of ils is pronounced z before a vowel, il-z-aiment. It is how you hear that the subject is plural.
Aimer is conjugated (ils aiment) and the second verb stays in the infinitive (danser).
Drop -er (étudi-) and add the vous ending -ez: vous étudiez.
Les enfants is plural, like ils, so the ending is -ent: les enfants jouent.

quiz.prompt: J'___ la radio dans la voiture. (écouter)
quiz.explanation: Écouter starts with a vowel, so je becomes j', and the je ending is -e: j'écoute.

quiz.prompt: The ending -ent in 'ils travaillent' is pronounced.
quiz.explanation: The -ent of a verb is always silent: ils travaillent sounds exactly like il travaille.
hints: Three of the six endings are silent.

guide.tip: Can't hear if it's il or ils? Listen for the z of the liaison: il aime, ils (z) aiment. With a consonant, only the context tells you.

concept.title: One verb, three English tenses
concept.markdown:
French has no *-ing* form for the present. **Je parle** means *I speak*, *I am speaking* and *I do speak*, all at once:

- **Je parle avec Paul.** (I'm talking with Paul.)
- **Je parle anglais.** (I speak English.)

conversations.title: New neighbours
conversations.scenario: Inès has just moved into a building in Lyon. On the stairs she meets Hugo, who lives across the landing.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Inès. J'habite ici depuis lundi.
lines.meaning: Hello! My name's Inès. I've lived here since Monday.
lines.note: j'habite: je becomes j' before a silent h

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Enchanté, Inès ! Moi, c'est Hugo. Tu travailles à Lyon ?
lines.meaning: Nice to meet you, Inès! I'm Hugo. Do you work in Lyon?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Oui, je travaille dans une librairie, près de la gare.
lines.meaning: Yes, I work in a bookshop, near the station.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Moi, j'étudie la musique à l'université.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, je chante dans un groupe avec deux amis.
lines.meaning: Yes, I sing in a band with two friends.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Moi, j'adore danser. J'écoute de la musique tout le temps.
lines.meaning: I love dancing. I listen to music all the time.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Alors, samedi, nous jouons dans un bar en ville.
lines.meaning: Well then, on Saturday we're playing in a bar in town.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Génial ! Vous jouez à quelle heure ?
lines.meaning: Great! What time are you playing?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: À neuf heures. Après, nous mangeons tous ensemble.
lines.meaning: At nine. Afterwards we all eat together.
lines.note: nous mangeons: the e keeps the g soft

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Parfait. J'aime beaucoup les nouveaux voisins !
lines.meaning: Perfect. I really like the new neighbours!

bites.title: Drop -er, add the ending
bites.rule: Take off -er and add -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent: parl- gives je parle, nous parlons, ils parlent.

bites.title: Three silent endings
bites.rule: -e, -es and -ent are silent: je parle, tu parles and ils parlent sound the same. Only -ons and -ez are heard.

bites.title: J' and the z of liaison
bites.rule: Before a vowel or silent h, je becomes j'. After nous, vous, ils, elles, the s sounds like z before a vowel.
bites.example: J'aime la musique. Ils aiment la musique.
bites.example_meaning: I like music. They like music.

bites.title: Nous mangeons
bites.rule: Verbs in -ger keep an e before -ons: nous mangeons, nous nageons. The e keeps the g soft.

sorts.title: Silent or heard?
sorts.why: -e, -es and -ent are never pronounced; -ons and -ez always are.

sorts.title: Je or j'?
sorts.why: Je becomes j' before a vowel or a silent h: j'aime, j'habite, j'écoute.

spots.why: Verbs in -ger keep the e before -ons.
After aimer, the second verb stays in the infinitive.
